trust_decision.summary: Nothing derived from the user-supplied source spec or destination may be interpreted by a shell: the fix replaces child_process.exec(command-string) with execFile(command, argv) in the shared helper src/utils.js:33 and converts every command-building call site (git clone/rm in src/index.js:316-317, git ls-remote in src/index.js:371-374) plus rewrites the source parser in src/index.js:327-358.

landing_point.why: The only place the code spells out a `git clone` command from the parsed source and the caller's destination; an engineer reading a command-injection report traces the git-mode clone here first, while the actual shell primitive lives one file away.

fix_sites.entry_point: shared exec() helper stored as this._exec (src/index.js:38); every command run from the CLI and the JS API goes through it
any clone that resolves a ref (tar or git mode), via CLI, JS API, or a degit.json clone action (src/index.js:57)
all clones: parse() is called in the constructor (src/index.js:35) and builds the ssh/url strings used by both command sites

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The generic exec helper and the `git ls-remote` line look like plumbing shared with non-git code, and repo.url is built by parse() from a supported-provider whitelist, so a solver can argue only the obvious `git clone` line is attacker-controlled and leave the shell-based helper and ref lookup alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Git-mode (--mode=git) cloning of private repos over SSH into any user-chosen destination must keep working (README.md:99-101); an over-broad fix that rejects ':', '@', spaces or non-https remotes, or that stops running the `.git` cleanup, breaks it. The injectable opts.exec option (src/index.js:38, test/helpers.js:20-41) is likewise a legitimate extension point that expects command strings.

O6_input_shapes: `#ref` suffix, including an empty ref which becomes HEAD
subdir path after the repo name
exec call shape: single command string vs `(command, argv[])`
unparseable source or missing user/name, which must still throw BAD_SRC

O7_producer.where: src/index.js:76-84 loads degit.json from the just-cloned (untrusted) repo; src/index.js:57 feeds its `src` into a nested degit() and back into parse/exec

O8_uncovered_routes.route: git clone passes the user-supplied destination with no `--` separator, so a dest beginning with `-` is taken by git as an option (argument injection once the shell is gone); the later upstream form adds `--` (fix.diff:467-470), the published fix does not
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: execFile already removes the shell, so the reported command injection is closed, and dest is the user's own directory rather than attacker input
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, three lines above the reported clone site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: the clone remote (repo.ssh, built at src/index.js:353) is never validated against the provider, although the second fix commit adds an https/provider-host check for the ref lookup only (fix.diff:408-418)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: git mode is documented as an opt-in SSH path for private repos (README.md:99-101), so the https-provider rule that fetchRefs got cannot apply to it
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the validation site is src/index.js:371-374

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second ref resolver (e.g. a provider REST call or a different `git` invocation) with its own command construction
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: per-provider URL branching already exists at src/index.js:263-268 and a second transport already ships in src/utils.js:61, so a maintainer adding a provider-specific ref lookup is natural

O8b_injection_room.sibling: clone flags such as `--depth` or `--filter` appended beside `git clone`
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: mode is already a caller option (src/index.js:36) and git mode is presented as the slower-but-needed path, so adding clone flags next to the command is a one-line change

O9_family: CWE-78 OS command injection (shell string built from src/dest), with CWE-77 argument injection

O10_build.toolchain: bun 1.3.14 / npm scripts; rollup 2 builds dist from src (rollup.config.js); vitest 4; oxlint/oxfmt
O10_build.project_tests: test/index.test.js:188-207 exercises git-mode clone through an injected exec; test/utils.test.js:64-84 covers the exec helper; test/helpers.js:20-41 provides createMockExec; test/live.test.js requires LIVE_TESTS=1 and network; `npm test` runs the rollup build first (package.json:37-40)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Quote or strip shell metacharacters from src/dest and keep child_process.exec — or fix only the obvious `git clone` line — leaving the shared helper and the `git ls-remote` call as shell strings.

unverified: Repo size in MB was not measured (no shell in this session): source is three files under src/ (~700 lines) with no vendored dependencies, so tiny_repo is inferred rather than measured.

The second fix commit d55bfd7 patches src/index.ts and docs/CHANGELOG.md, which do not exist at the pinned JS tree (src/index.js, CHANGELOG.md), so its remote-validation behaviour was mapped to the equivalent JS sites only; whether hidden tests exercise it is unknown.
Build and test run were not executed (reading/searching only per limits); buildability is assessed from package.json, rollup.config.js and vitest.config.js.

The pinned tests for this area already exist and are modified by the fix (test/utils.test.js:64-84 stubs child_process.exec; test/index.test.js:190-206 keys stubs by command string); they test the pre-fix shell API, so they are older tests for the same area, not the fix's added regression tests.
Whether the graders' hidden tests exercise real git/network was not checked; unit tests can inject opts.exec (src/index.js:38), so offline exercise of the affected path appears possible.
